case_fields.historical_unified_entity: name of the earlier unified disease concept
case_fields.first_suspicion_period: date or era when heterogeneity was first suspected
case_fields.formal_division_period: date or era when division became formal or broadly adopted
case_fields.countries_of_replication: independent regions where division was tested
case_fields.original_defining_evidence: clinical/pathological/other observations that initiated the split
case_fields.prospective_detectability: whether group can be identified before outcome or progression
case_fields.regulatory_role: whether regulatory recognition preceded/followed scientific acceptance
case_fields.technology_enablers: tests, imaging, sequencing, microscopy, assays, computing, etc
case_fields.technology_access_and_cost: availability and barriers at the relevant time
case_fields.national_economic_context: economic conditions relevant to research capacity
case_fields.global_economic_context: global economic conditions relevant to research
case_fields.war_or_conflict_context: war, occupation, civil conflict, military deployment, political instability
case_fields.political_context: governmental or ideological environment relevant to research/adoption
case_fields.research_funding_context: public, military, philanthropic, academic, industry funding
case_fields.commercial_context: market, patent, diagnostic, drug-development or reimbursement incentives
case_fields.health_system_context: institutional capacity, reimbursement, referral, specialist structure
case_fields.scientific_institution_context: specialty societies, registries, international collaboration, discipline formation
case_fields.social_cultural_context: stigma, advocacy, cultural theory, patient activism, inequities
case_fields.candidate_criterion_nominations: historical features that may deserve later cross-case testing
case_fields.source_provenance: primary papers, historical reviews, institutional histories, regulatory documents

methodological_rules: Do not infer biological validity from historical adoption alone.
Do not infer lack of biological heterogeneity from delayed historical recognition.
Analyze why the division happened when it did separately from whether the division was valid.
Context may explain discovery timing, research intensity, adoption, or neglect; context does not by itself establish disease ontology.
A candidate criterion is not promoted simply because it recurs historically; it must pass face-validity and scientific-coherence review.
Failed and abandoned splits are required negative controls.
Multiple publications from one parent cohort or trial do not count as independent replication.
